rv.q: But Robert Falls’ production drains much of the humor, urgency and anxiety from the piece, letting it amble along like an inflated actors’ exercise in sustaining atmosphere without action.
American Buffalo stings the heart now the way it undoubtedly once did the ear.

cn.t: This revival of Mamet's classic receives mixed reviews, with critics finding the production fails to fully capture the profane poetry and poignant desperation that make the play work when done right.

vs.sum: The Belasco Theatre offers stunning ambiance with its historic Tiffany lamps and stained-glass ceiling, but suffers from tight legroom typical of older venues. While sound quality is generally good, sightlines can be inconsistent, especially from side orchestra seats.

acc.note: 8 wheelchair locations in Orchestra. Induction loops for t-coil hearing aids. Infrared devices available.
